title: Manual Testing: Keyboard, Zoom & Colour 🧪
description: Perform essential manual checks that automated tools miss: keyboard flow, 200% zoom, and contrast inspection.

slides.title: The Manual Testing Mindset 🤔
slides.content:
Manual testing is about experiencing the site as different users. You need to:

- Disconnect your mouse.
- Zoom in to 200%.
- Turn off images.
- Disable CSS or apply high contrast.
- Use a screen reader (next lesson).

The goal: catch what automated tools cannot see – like confusing tab order, focus loss, or missing visible focus.

quizData.question: Which of the following cannot be detected by an automated tool?
quizData.explanation: Focus order requires human judgment to determine if it matches visual/functional expectations.

slides.title: Keyboard Testing Checklist ⌨️
slides.content:
1. **Tab through the entire page** – can you reach every interactive element?
2. **Shift+Tab** to go backward – does it work symmetrically?
3. **Focus never disappears** – is there always a visible focus indicator?
4. **No keyboard traps** – can you always Tab away from a component (except modals)?
5. **Skip link** – is it functional and first in tab order?
6. **Custom widgets** – do they follow standard patterns (arrow keys in menus)?

slides.title: Quick Test: Tab Through
slides.codeSnippet:
<!-- Open your page, click address bar, press Tab repeatedly.
Ask: Can I operate everything? Can I tell where I am? -->

quizData.question: You Tab through a page and focus jumps to a button at the bottom before going back to the middle. Is this an accessibility issue?

options.text: Yes, focus order should be logical and predictable

quizData.explanation: WCAG 2.4.3 requires a meaningful sequence. Jumping around disorients users.

slides.title: Zoom & Responsive Reflow 🔍
slides.content:
Zoom your browser to 200% (Ctrl/Cmd + +). Check:

- No horizontal scrolling is required (content wraps/reflows).
- All text remains readable (no cut‑off).
- Interactive elements are still reachable and usable.
- No overlapping content.

Additionally, resize the viewport to 320px wide (smallest phone). The site should still work.

quizData.question: At 200% zoom, what must NOT happen for a site to pass WCAG AA?

options.text: Horizontal scrolling appears and content is lost

quizData.explanation: Content must reflow within a 320px equivalent width without horizontal scroll.

slides.title: Colour & Contrast Checks 🎨
slides.content:
Use a contrast checker to verify text/background pairs. Also:

- **Toggle high contrast mode** (Windows) or use the 'prefers‑contrast' media query.
- **View the site in greyscale** (DevTools rendering → Emulate vision deficiencies → Achromatopsia).
- Check that information conveyed with colour is also conveyed in another way.

Never rely on colour alone to communicate status.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Create a manual testing script
Write down a series of steps for each test. Use the same script each time you test, so you don't forget anything.
